title: Zephyrine and the Choir
premise: Cyrus Vane has spent her life as a smuggler and mapmaker, erasing herself from every record in the Thornfell mountains—until a prophecy written a century ago names her by her true, forgotten name. The prophecy foretells that on the night of the Choir's singing, the court beneath the mountain will claim a soul sold to them long ago: her own, bargained away by the mother she barely remembers. To survive, Cyrus must descend into the Undercourt with a disgraced choir mistress and a debt-collector who knows too much about her past, navigating courts where music is law and names are currency. In the climax she discovers the soul sold was not hers but her twin sister's, still singing in the Choir—and she must choose between reclaiming her own survival and freeing the sister whose existence was erased to save her. Cyrus gives up her invisibility forever, trading her name into the prophecy so both sisters walk out of the mountain, changed and bound together.
about_author: A. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing obscure folk song collections before turning to fantasy. They write stories about people who survive by staying unnoticed, and live somewhere rainy with an unreasonable number of maps.

chapters.title: The Unmapped Road
chapters.summary: Cyrus Vane guides a smuggling caravan through a pass that officially does not exist, demonstrating her mastery of Thornfell's hidden geography. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: confident competence shadowed by loneliness—she knows every road except the one back to belonging.

chapters.title: A Name in Old Ink
chapters.summary: In a bookbinder's shop, Cyrus finds a century-old prophecy ledger listing tonight's date beside her true name—a name she didn't know she had. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: vertigo; her carefully constructed invisibility shatters in a single line of ink.

chapters.title: What the Landlady Knows
chapters.summary: Cyrus confronts Marla, the landlady who raised her, and learns only fragments: a bargain, a fire, a mother who fled. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve—the family she trusted kept the truth from her.

chapters.title: The Debt-Collector's Offer
chapters.summary: Sable Quill, an elegant collector for the Undercourt, finds Cyrus and offers passage beneath the mountain—if she surrenders willingly at the next full moon. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: predatory charm masking genuine curiosity about the girl who erased herself.

chapters.title: The Choir Mistress
chapters.summary: Cyrus seeks Odile Ferrant, a disgraced former choir mistress exiled from the Undercourt, and persuades her to guide the descent in exchange for revenge. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: two wounded women striking a wary alliance neither fully trusts.

chapters.title: Songs Are Contracts
chapters.summary: Odile teaches Cyrus the laws of the Undercourt: every song is binding, every name is currency, and silence is the only shield. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: humbling education; her mapmaker's confidence is useless against rules made of sound.

chapters.title: The Toll Gate of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: The trio enters the mountain through a smuggler's gate and pays a toll in memories; Sable loses something he pretends not to mourn. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: first crack in his composure, hinting at what the court holds over him.

chapters.title: The Market of Borrowed Voices
chapters.summary: In the Undercourt's bazaar, voices are bought and sold; Cyrus hears a singer whose voice is achingly familiar. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: uncanny longing she cannot explain, planting the seed of the twin revelation.

chapters.title: Rules of the Court Beneath
chapters.summary: The party navigates a formal audience with a minor lord, where one misstep in etiquette means enslavement; Odile's old rank saves them. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: bitter nostalgia—returning to the court that cast her out.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Souls
chapters.summary: Breaking into the soul-archive, Cyrus finds the contract bearing her name—but the signature is dated the day after her recorded birth. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: wrongness deepening; the dates don't fit the story she's been told.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable reveals he was once human, his own voice sold to buy his brother's freedom; he warns Cyrus the court never releases what it truly owns. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: reluctant honesty forging real trust between enemies.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for the End of the World
chapters.summary: The Choir rehearses the centennial Song that renews the court's power; Cyrus infiltrates as a stagehand and hears the voice from the market again. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: dread and recognition braided together—the voice sounds like her own.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Was Erased
chapters.summary: Odile confirms it: Cyrus had a twin, Wren, whose existence was traded to the court so Cyrus could live free. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: devastating reversal—Cyrus's whole life was purchased with someone else's.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Cyrus meets Wren, lead singer of the Choir, who remembers nothing of the surface and resents this stranger claiming her story. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: furious grief; the rescued may not want rescuing.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Wren refuses escape: leaving would unravel the Song holding the mountain's refugees safe. Cyrus must weigh her sister's freedom against hundreds of lives. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: moral collapse of Cyrus's simple mission into an impossible choice.

chapters.title: Marla's Confession
chapters.summary: Through a scrying mirror, Marla confesses the original bargain: she was the midwife who offered one twin to save the other, and has regretted it for thirty years. POV: Marla. Emotional beat: guilt finally spoken aloud; forgiveness neither asked nor granted.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Prophecy
chapters.summary: Cyrus realizes prophecies are contracts, and contracts can be amended—if someone with standing signs. She begins forging an amendment with Odile's expertise and Sable's legal knowledge. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: hope through audacity; the mapmaker starts redrawing fate itself.

chapters.title: The Night of the Choir
chapters.summary: The centennial performance begins; the court's lords gather, and Cyrus slips into the Choir wearing Wren's stolen role. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose as she steps onto the stage of her own doom.

chapters.title: The Song That Names You
chapters.summary: Mid-performance, the Song demands its due and speaks Cyrus's true name before the court; she answers by singing the forged amendment, offering her name instead of either sister's soul. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: climactic self-sacrifice—invisibility abandoned, identity weaponized.

chapters.title: Two Voices, One Contract
chapters.summary: The court accepts the amendment only if sung in harmony; Wren joins her, their blended voices rewriting the terms so both walk free while the refugee-sustaining Song passes to a willing new chorus. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: reconciliation through music; the sisters choose each other.

chapters.title: Exit Through the Mapped World
chapters.summary: The three emerge into dawn above Thornfell; Sable, freed by the amended contract, chooses exile over return. Cyrus draws a new map—one that marks the way home instead of hiding it. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: quiet release; debts paid, futures unscripted.

chapters.title: Zephyrine
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Cyrus—Zephyrine now, by choice—opens a shop selling honest maps, with Wren teaching songs that bind no one. A customer asks if she fears being found. She says no. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: resolution and belonging; visibility embraced at last.
